thread:
maria: Heads-up — noticed quota attribution mismatch in the console for Dedicated pools when the SDK sends a route header. Dashboard shows requests landing in the shared pool instead of tenant-reserved. Repro steps below.

samir: Can you paste a minimal request? Which header key are you sending?

maria: Example (redacted):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate 
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer REDACT' 
  -H 'x-route-affinity: team-162' 
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
  -d '{"model":"rw-large-v1","input":"hi"}'
```

kevin: Quick thought — platform expects `x-route-hint` historically. I think some SDKs started emitting `x-route-affinity` and TS recently moved to `x-route-tag`. Could be a header-normalization/aliasing gap in the proxy.

jess: We rolled out header aliasing in the proxy last week to support older clients. If the alias mapping failed here the console would still read the internal canonical tag and attribute to shared.

maria: Observed across py-sdk 0.12.7 and ts-sdk 2.3.0. Py sends `x-route-affinity`, TS sends `x-route-tag`. Both end up billed from shared pool. Logs: requests show route="" when they should be route="team-162".

samir: Can you paste the redacted headers from a failed request?

maria: Headers snippet:
```
Authorization: REDACT
x-route-affinity: team-162
x-client-version: py-0.12.7
User-Agent: redwood-py/0.12.7
```

infra-monitor: FYI alert — routing-service saw a parsing spike at 14:03 UTC: stack trace indicates header_normalize -> nil pointer while mapping aliases. Rolling 5xxs at the same time. :eyes:

kevin: Ok that stack trace matches a bug where we canonicalize header names via net/http (Go) which uppercases first letters (e.g., `X-Route-Affinity`). Our normalizer lowercases but only checks for exact strings; alias `X-Route-Tag` didn't match and fell through.

jess: Proposed short-term fix: normalize by lowercasing all incoming header keys and then map a small alias table -> canonical internal key. Add unit tests for `X-Route-*` variants. Small canary rolling patch.

maria: :thumbsup: Prefer a proxy-side fix so we don't force immediate SDK churn. But we should coordinate with SDK teams to emit canonical header names for stability.

samir: For SDKs we can emit both canonical and legacy aliases for 2 releases (dual-write) to give us breathing room. I'll open tickets for py/ts/go SDKs to add fallback header emission.

kevin: I'll open a PR for proxy normalization + tests. Plan to canary in us-east-1 at 10% traffic. Console team — expect attribution to flip for the canary window.

jess: Confirmed. Canary scheduled. Console & billing: heads-up that per-route counts may flip transiently during rollout.

maria: Concern: quota-metering is per-route; if attribution flips mid-window customers might see double-billing or unexpected usage. We should consider freezing reconciliation or flagging affected customers.

samir: Agreed. I'll coordinate with billing to hold reconciliation for the impacted windows and add an alert if per-route usage delta > 20% vs baseline.

console-bot: Deployment planned: proxy-normalize-headers v1.0.1 -> canary us-east-1 at 2026-03-21T15:10Z :rocket:

kevin: Thanks. I'll also ping SDK leads to emit aliases and add a short note in release notes about header deprecation timeline.

maria: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: PR links, SDK tickets, billing freeze plan. I'll open a short doc with timeline and rollback plan.
